basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Mense secundo, vigesima septima die mensis arefacta est terra. Supra dictum est quod'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Mense secundo, vigesima septima die mensis arefacta est terra. Supra dictum est quod primo mense inchoante exsiccata esset superficies terrae; et nunc mense secundo pene completo arefacta esse terra describitur, quia nimirum tunc in superficie virentibus herbis tellus exsiccata est, ut posset revirescere, atque herbas, quas absumpserat aqua, denuo germinare. Nunc vero in tantum etiam interius arefacta est, ut calcantium gressus sustineret, in tantum herbis vestita florentibus, ut etiam pascendis esset idonea pecoribus ac jumentis.
